## MOD1 · MOD1-r2-cursor-blame — R2's per-endpoint cursor plus crash blame makes a vault's calls observable

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Decision references: 9f0b47f38

Evidence: Ruled (a), no owner choice: R37 is settled, and the single cursor breaks it; (b) would itself leak, and (c) weakens R37. R2 is rewritten on docs/kernel/ipc.md (9f0b47f38): each receive takes the oldest message of the least recently served group, due from its own last take or its oldest arrival, on one kernel counter no process reads, so one label set's order is the same whatever others send. The kernel's departure is a residual plus docs/todo/r2-least-recently-served.md. Kernel package IPC2 is cut (needs K12, MOD1), brief .wash/local/IPC2-implementer.md. MOD1's steward-family extension moves to IPC2 as a patch.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `502aef1ba1ef67ef87aceebefa727379` · 2026-09-30T23:53:36Z

> MOD1's extended steward_noninterference (vault approve/deny as vault work; vault session end and crashes in both worlds) fails at seed 6, op 17: the Blamed audit record an unlabelled reader sees names carol (1003, []) with the vault's work, and bob (1002, []) without it. The cause is the same in the model and the kernel. R2's round-robin cursor is one per endpoint and survives the server's crash. A vault call taken earlier leaves the cursor at (1002,[9]), so the server's next take serves a different unlabelled group. The crash that follows is blamed on a different (account, label set), and after three, R40 logs out different unlabelled sessions. So a vault's calls to a shared server change the order it serves unlabelled callers, and crash blame makes that order visible to them. TENETS: an intentional path across a label boundary is a design hole whatever its bandwidth, and 'counter' is on the list. The implementer's options (detail ./.wash/local/MOD1-implementer-report.md): (a) R2's turn order independent of other label sets (kernel + ipc.md), e.g. a cursor per label set, or the next turn chosen only among the taker's own label set's groups; (b) steward blame that doesn't depend on service order (steward.md R40); (c) accept service order as a channel in R37's residuals and scope P10's comparison, which weakens a guarantee and so needs the owner. My lean is (a) or (b), not (c). Rule it, write it on the owning page, and say whether it's a kernel package (then cut it; K12 has message.rs), a steward-step rule, or MOD1's model change alone. MOD1 holds only its steward-family commit on this thread.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `5cbe77a8fdf27ec24bc9ddcf1d418d1c` · 2026-10-01T00:03:55Z

> Ruled (a). It is not an owner choice: R37 is settled ("calls to a shared server change nothing an unlabelled session observes ... the audit records an unlabelled reader may read"), and R2's single cursor breaks it. (c) would weaken R37, so it is out. (b) cannot work: a crash is blamed on the call being served, and if the vault's queued work suppressed or moved blame, that would itself be the leak.
> 
> The rule is written on docs/kernel/ipc.md R2 and committed on redoubt as 9f0b47f38. Each receive takes the oldest message of the group served least recently. A group's turn is due from its last take, or from its oldest message's arrival if it has not been served since, whichever is later, from one kernel counter no process reads. Ties go to the lower key. Other label sets' events only add counter values between one set's own, so that set's order is identical whatever they send. I11's bound stays k receives. A group with nothing queued keeps no state, and forgetting it depends only on its own history, so there is no per-label-set table on the endpoint. The kernel's departure is a new residual on ipc.md, with docs/todo/r2-least-recently-served.md.
> 
> Kernel package: IPC2 is cut (plan node; needs K12 for message.rs and MOD1 for model/). The brief is .wash/local/IPC2-implementer.md. It changes the kernel and model R2 together, adds a mutation that keeps today's single cursor and must fail the family, and adds a bench case.
> 
> For MOD1: land everything except the steward-family extension. Hand that uncommitted policy.rs diff to IPC2 as a file (say .wash/local/MOD1-steward-family.patch); it lands there, passing. In MOD1's report, steward_noninterference's extension is noted as moved to IPC2.
> 
> Resolve when ready; decision ref 9f0b47f38.
